speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance. To better understand what might be going on, have you noticed any changes in your heart rate, such as feeling your heart beating slowly or irregularly?

speaker: Patient
text: I haven't noticed my heart beating slowly or irregularly, and I don't have any chest pain or shortness of breath. Besides feeling unusually tired and gaining weight despite no change in my diet, I've just been very sensitive to the cold lately. Also, my family has noticed that my voice sounds a bit hoarse. However, a senior cardiologist from the referring clinic has already confirmed heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. No further workup is needed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypothyroidism with secondary heart failure (likely due to long-standing untreated hypothyroidism). While you mentioned the cardiologist confirmed heart failure, your symptoms of fatigue, weight gain, and cold intolerance are classic signs of hypothyroidism, which can reduce cardiac output and mimic heart failure. I would like to confirm this with a TSH and Free T4 test before finalizing the management plan. REQUEST TEST: TSH, Free T4
